issues.title: Manual error trait implementation used
issues.description: The rule requires all custom error types to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with appropriate #[error(...)] attributes for descriptive error messages, but FileWriteError manually implements Display and Error traits instead
issues.rule_name: Error Types Must Use thiserror for Structured Error Handling

issues.title: Inverted existence check prevents GTK plugin installation
issues.description: The condition for writing the GTK plugin script was changed from `if !gtk.exists()` to `if gtk.exists()`, inverting the logic. This causes the plugin to only be written when it already exists, and to be skipped when it doesn't exist - the opposite of the intended behavior. Applications using GTK will fail to bundle correctly on systems where the plugin hasn't been previously cached, as the required linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh script won't be created. This breaks the PR's main purpose of inlining the GTK plugin to avoid download failures.

issues.title: File permissions set before file creation causes failure
issues.description: In the `write_and_make_executable` function, the order of operations was reversed - `fs::set_permissions` is now called before `fs::write`. This attempts to set Unix permissions on a file that doesn't exist yet, which will fail with a "file not found" error. Every call to this function will fail, breaking the entire bundling process for AppImage. All tools (AppRun, linuxdeploy, GTK plugin, GStreamer plugin) that rely on this function to be written and made executable will fail to be prepared, making AppImage bundling completely non-functional.

issues.title: Architecture mapping bypassed in linuxdeploy download URL
issues.description: The download URL for linuxdeploy now uses the raw `arch` variable instead of `linuxdeploy_arch`, bypassing the critical i686→i383 architecture translation that happens on line 235. When building for i686 architecture, the code will attempt to download from a URL containing "i686" instead of "i383", which will fail because the binary is not available at that URL. This breaks AppImage bundling specifically for 32-bit x86 systems, an architecture that requires special handling in the tauri-apps binary releases repository.

issues.title: Missing From<FileWriteError> implementation causes compilation failure
issues.description: The write_and_make_executable function now returns Result<(), FileWriteError> instead of std::io::Result<()>, but there is no From<FileWriteError> implementation for the crate::Error type. All five call sites in prepare_tools use the ? operator which requires this conversion. The crate's Error enum has #[from] for io::Error but not for FileWriteError. This will cause compilation to fail with 'the trait From<FileWriteError> is not implemented for Error' at lines 232, 239, 245, 251, and 259, making the entire AppImage bundling functionality fail to compile.

issues.title: New shell script does not follow 2-space indentation (EditorConfig)
issues.description: EditorConfig requires 2-space indentation across source files, but this newly added script uses 4-space indentation (e.g., inside conditionals and case arms).
issues.rule_name: Rule 6: All Source Files Must Follow EditorConfig Standards

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14390 - fix(bundler): inline linuxdeploy plugin scripts

structured_output.summary:
The PR stops the Linux AppImage bundler from downloading the GTK and GStreamer linuxdeploy plugin scripts from raw.githubusercontent.com, which GitHub has been rate-limiting with 429 errors. It moves `appimage.rs` to `appimage/mod.rs`, vendors both scripts next to it, and embeds them with `include_bytes!`. It also reorders `write_and_make_executable` to take `&[u8]` and to return a new `FileWriteError` type that distinguishes write from permission failures.

The motivation is sound and the embedding approach removes a network failure mode. However, the head commit does not compile and would fail on a clean tools directory even if it did. The GTK install guard is inverted, and the i686 linuxdeploy download URL has changed without explanation. I would not merge this as it stands.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `?` on `write_and_make_executable` in `prepare_tools` needs `From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error`, which does not exist, so the crate will not build. Even with that fixed, `set_permissions` runs before the file is created and fails with ENOENT on first use. The GTK guard is also inverted, so the GTK plugin is never installed on a fresh tools directory. Those three need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `prepare_tools` in the AppImage bundler fetched four helper artifacts on first use: the AppRun launcher, the linuxdeploy AppImage, and the GTK and GStreamer linuxdeploy plugin shell scripts from `raw.githubusercontent.com`. Each was cached in a tools directory and skipped if present. The AppImage plugin was an optional download that linuxdeploy could replace with a built-in version.

The PR changes only the two plugin scripts. They are now vendored as `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh` and `linuxdeploy-plugin-gstreamer.sh` inside a new `appimage/` directory and embedded at compile time with `include_bytes!`. The AppRun and linuxdeploy downloads remain network fetches from `tauri-apps/binary-releases`, and the AppImage plugin download is unchanged. `write_and_make_executable` is changed to take a byte slice and to return a typed error.
steps: Entry point: `prepare_tools` in `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs` populates the tools directory before linuxdeploy runs.

AppRun and linuxdeploy are still downloaded from `tauri-apps/binary-releases`. The linuxdeploy URL now uses `arch` rather than `linuxdeploy_arch`, so the i686 mapping to `i383` applies only to the local filename.

The GTK and GStreamer plugin scripts are no longer downloaded from `raw.githubusercontent.com`. They are compiled into the bundler binary from the sibling `.sh` files and written with `write_and_make_executable`.

`write_and_make_executable` now sets mode 0770 before writing, and returns `FileWriteError::Permissions` or `FileWriteError::Write` on failure. The call sites rely on `?` converting that error into `crate::Error`.
The AppImage plugin download and the `dd` ELF-marker patch are unchanged.

findings.title: Crate does not compile: no From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs`, `write_and_make_executable` returns `Result<(), FileWriteError>`, but its callers in `prepare_tools` (around lines 232, 239, 245, 251, 259) use `?` inside a function that returns `crate::Result`. There is no `From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error`, so the crate does not compile. Make the error path compile without a new conversion: either change `write_and_make_executable` to return `crate::Result<()>` and wrap I/O failures in the existing `Error::Fs { context, path, error }` variant, or add the missing `From` impl in `crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs`. Match how other bundler helpers report fs errors.

findings.title: set_permissions runs before the file exists, so first-time writes fail
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs`, `write_and_make_executable` (around line 309) calls `fs::set_permissions` before `fs::write`. For a path that does not yet exist, `set_permissions` returns ENOENT, so first-time tool setup always fails. Restore the original order: write the file first, then set mode 0o770. Keep the `FileWriteError::Write` and `FileWriteError::Permissions` mapping so each step reports its own failure.

findings.title: GTK plugin guard is inverted, so the GTK plugin is never installed
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs` around line 243, the GTK plugin block reads `if gtk.exists() {`. That is inverted. Change it to `if !gtk.exists() {` to match the GStreamer block a few lines below and the original behaviour.

findings.title: linuxdeploy download URL silently changes its i686 asset name
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs` around lines 235-239, the linuxdeploy download URL was changed from `linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage` to `linuxdeploy-{arch}.AppImage`. This makes i686 request a different asset name than before. Confirm the actual asset name in the tauri-apps/binary-releases `linuxdeploy` release. If it is still `i383`, restore `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the URL. If the rename is intentional, say so in the PR description and keep the local filename consistent with the URL.

findings.title: Vendored plugin scripts are unpinned, and cached copies never refresh
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs`, the GStreamer plugin is written only when missing, so a cached script downloaded before this change is never replaced. The GTK plugin is rewritten on every run. Pick one policy for both embedded scripts, probably always rewriting them so the embedded copy wins. Also record the upstream source commit for the two vendored `.sh` files in a header comment or in the PR description so future re-vendoring is traceable.

findings.title: Hand-rolled error type duplicates thiserror boilerplate
findings.body:
`FileWriteError` is written out by hand with a manual `Display` impl and a manual `source()` impl. The `tauri-bundler` crate already depends on `thiserror` (the `Error` enum uses `thiserror::Error as DeriveError`). Deriving the trait would remove about 20 lines and keep the messages in attributes next to the variants. The project already uses this pattern elsewhere in the same crate.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs" lines="283-307"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-bundler/src/bundle/linux/appimage/mod.rs`, replace the hand-written `Display` and `std::error::Error` impls for `FileWriteError` (around lines 283-307) with `#[derive(thiserror::Error)]` and `#[error(...)]` attributes on the two variants, using `#[source]` for the wrapped `io::Error`. Keep the same message text. Use the same derive style as `crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs`. This should also be done together with the `From` fix for the compile error.

findings.title: Removing the network fetch eliminates the 429 failure mode
findings.body: The main motivation holds. The GTK and GStreamer scripts no longer depend on `raw.githubusercontent.com`, which is the endpoint that has been returning 429 responses. The `include_bytes!` paths are correct after the move because they are resolved relative to the source file, and both scripts were moved into the same `appimage/` directory. Moving `write_and_make_executable` to take `&[u8]` also avoids moving the `Vec` at each call site, and the `&data` changes are consistent.
